_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Samoa covering Polynesian settlement (~1000 BCE, 'Cradle of Polynesia', Lapita people), Samoan Empire (Tu'i Manu'a dynasty, oral tradition claims 3000+ years), European contact (Jacob Roggeveen 1722), missionary arrival (John Williams LMS 1830), Tripartite Convention 1899 (Germany took Western Samoa, US took Eastern/American Samoa), German Samoa (1900-1914), New Zealand mandate (1914-1962), Mau movement (non-violent independence, Lauaki Namulau'ulu, Black Saturday 1929), independence 1962 (first Pacific island nation), fa'a Samoa (Samoan Way), 2011 International Date Line switch.

religion.note: Deeply Christian (97%+, among most devout in world); Congregational Christian Church of Samoa (CCCS/EFKS, largest, LMS missionary legacy 1830, village pastor central to social hierarchy); Catholic (Marist Brothers); LDS/Mormons (massive growth, 16.9%, among highest % globally, temples, returned missionaries influence); to'ona'i (Sunday sabbath, no work/sport/swimming, family feast, church all day, strictly observed); pastor (faife'au) holds enormous social power; fa'a Samoa integrates Christianity deeply; village fine system enforces church attendance

ethnic_groups.name: Samoan
ethnic_groups.notes: Polynesian; fa'a Samoa ('The Samoan Way', comprehensive cultural system: matai chiefly system, 'aiga extended family, village fono council, communal land 80%+ customary, feagaiga sacred brother-sister covenant, tautua service); matai (chiefs, ~25k titles, elected by family, control village governance, only matai could vote until 1990 universal suffrage); Samoan tatau (pe'a male full-body tattoo thigh-to-knee, malu female, painful/sacred, identity marker, word 'tattoo' derived from Polynesian tatau); 'Cradle of Polynesia' (Samoa considered ancestral homeland from which Eastern Polynesia settled); rugby (passion, Manu Samoa, many play for NZ/Australia due to diaspora); fire knife dance (siva afi); ava ceremony (kava); extremely homogeneous ethnically

ethnic_groups.name: Part-Samoan (Euronesian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed European-Samoan; historical trading/missionary families; afakasi; often prominent in business/politics

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (~1k, small business, historical, 1890s coolie labour, Apia); European (~500); American Samoa connection (US territory, similar culture, free movement, ~55k, many cross-border families); massive diaspora (~300k Samoans abroad vs 226k in Samoa: New Zealand ~182k, Australia ~75k, US ~56k, American Samoa ~55k; remittances ~25% GDP)

country_profile.time_zone: WST (UTC+13) / WSDT (UTC+14); switched from UTC-11 in December 2011

independence.from: New Zealand UN trusteeship (first Pacific island nation to gain independence in 20th century)

country_profile.notes_unique: First Pacific island nation independent (January 1, 1962, from NZ trusteeship; preceded by Tonga's continuous sovereignty); fa'a Samoa ('The Samoan Way', comprehensive cultural system governing every aspect of life: matai/chiefly authority, fono/village council, 'aiga/extended family, communal land ownership, tautua/service obligation, not merely tradition but living governance parallel to Western law); Mau movement (1920s-30s, non-violent independence movement, Lauaki Namulau'ulu Mamoe exiled by Germans; Black Saturday December 28, 1929, NZ police shot dead 11 Samoans including chief Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III who called 'My blood has been spilt for Samoa, I am proud to give it' as he died, NZ apologised 2002); International Date Line switch (December 29, 2011 skipped entirely, moved from UTC-11 to UTC+13, gained a day to align with Australia/NZ trade partners instead of US); Robert Louis Stevenson (Scottish author, lived in Samoa 1889-94, died/buried on Mount Vaea Apia, called 'Tusitala' storyteller by Samoans, Vailima estate now museum); tatau (Samoan full-body tattoo tradition, pe'a for men thigh-to-knee, malu for women, extremely painful, rite of passage, identity, word 'tattoo' from Polynesian, UNESCO); Samoan rugby (Manu Samoa, punches above weight, many NZ/Australian/English internationals are Samoan-heritage); diaspora larger than homeland (~300k abroad vs 226k home, NZ largest Polynesian city Auckland); to'ona'i Sunday (absolute sabbath, village fines for breaking); 2009 tsunami (September 29, 8.1 earthquake, 143 dead, devastating, Lalomanu); matai system (elected chiefs control family resources/land/representation, ~25k titles, parallel governance); twin Samoas (Samoa/Western vs American Samoa/US territory, culturally identical, politically divided by 1899 treaty, free movement)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Fiame Naomi Mata'afa
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: FAST (Fa'atuatua i le Atua Samoa ua Tasi); first female PM; daughter of Samoa's first PM (Mata'afa dynasty); elected in dramatic constitutional crisis (2021 election tied 25-25-1, speaker refused to convene parliament, sworn in under tent outside locked Parliament, Supreme Court upheld, O le Ao o le Malo/Head of State eventually recognised her); ended HRPP's 22-year dominance; governance reformer; anti-China port project

head_of_state.name: Tuimaleali'ifano Va'aletoa Sualauvi II
head_of_state.title: O le Ao o le Malo (Head of State)
head_of_state.notes: Ceremonial; holds one of four paramount tama-a-'aiga (royal son) chiefly titles; 5-year terms elected by Parliament; constitutional role similar to president/governor-general

former_leaders.name: Tuilaepa Sa'ilele Malielegaoi
former_leaders.notes: HRPP; 22+ years (longest-serving Pacific leader); dominated Samoan politics; authoritarian tendencies (constitutional amendments, media control); China port deal (controversial); refused to concede 2021 election (constitutional crisis, eventually stepped down after court rulings); former finance minister; development-focused but democratic erosion concerns

former_leaders.name: Tofilau Eti Alesana
former_leaders.notes: HRPP founder; introduced VAT (VAGST); economic reforms; died in office 1999

former_leaders.name: Mata'afa Fiame Mulinu'u II
former_leaders.notes: First PM at independence (January 1, 1962); paramount chief; died later in 1962; father of current PM Fiame Naomi Mata'afa; founding father
